sanskrit_verse:
तत् प्रजापालनं प्रोक्तं त्रिविधं न्यायवेदिभिः ।
परचक्राच् चौरभयाद् बलिनोऽन्यायवर्तिनः ॥
transliteration:
tat prajāpālanaṃ proktaṃ trividhaṃ nyāyavedibhiḥ |
paracakrāc caurabhayād balino'nyāyavartinaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The protection of subjects is declared in three forms by those who know Dharma: from external threats, from fear of thieves, and from the unjust actions of the powerful.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from the capacity to protect consciousness, not coerce it.
Causation arises from identifying root threats to societal integrity.
Capacity-based responsibility assigns protective duty to those capable of enforcement.
Restoration logic prioritizes re-establishing safety over assigning blame.
Consciousness alignment requires a society free from fear and domination.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a subject group reports systemic threat THEN assign protective oversight to nearest capable authority.
IF theft or raiding behavior is detected THEN deploy preventive containment without punitive intent.
IF power-holder acts against Dharma THEN initiate consciousness realignment protocol before structural correction.
IF fear is reported among citizens THEN immediate restoration of security protocols MUST activate.
IF imbalance in protection is observed THEN redistribute guardianship based on actual capacity.
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme level, this verse establishes that judicial review must include assessment of whether authorities are fulfilling their tripartite protection duties. Courts must evaluate not just legality but also efficacy in shielding citizens from external aggression, internal predation, and misuse of power. The threshold of responsibility lies in demonstrable failure to maintain these protections.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Nyaya here functions as the recognition of sequential threats—external, internal, and positional—and addresses them through proportional response aimed at restoring balance. There is no punitive element; rather, each threat triggers a completion process: containment for aggression, rehabilitation for theft, and realignment for abuse of power. Responsibility flows from capability, not fault.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Deployment of neutralizing shields to prevent further harm from aggressors.
Initiation of resource-return cycles to reverse losses caused by theft.
Activation of consciousness-reeducation programs for power-abusers prior to role reassignment.
Implementation of community-wide fear-dissolution practices upon threat removal.
Reconstruction of governance structures where protective failures occurred.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Protection is executed not through punishment but through alignment with consciousness. Justice restores reality, not vengeance. Dharma prevails through awareness, not force.
